body.x: In power plants and process plants, routine inspections take workers into areas with high temperatures, loud noise and confined spaces, and results can differ from one inspector to the next.
Could a robot handle the repetitive patrols and leave people to decide what to do about what it finds?

A-PRO Co., Ltd., an Anyang-based power conversion company founded in 2000 and led by CEO Jonghyun Lim, answers with APRISM Facility, which it is showcasing at KES 2026. The company says it wants to secure more proof-of-concept (PoC) and field demonstration references with Korean power generators, utilities and plant operators, and to identify joint demonstrations with overseas utilities and local partners.

APRISM Facility puts visual, thermal imaging and acoustic sensor payloads on a quadruped robot that patrols a facility on its own, while AI analyzes the data in real time. It checks whether workers wear required protective equipment, spots visible equipment abnormalities, detects water, oil and gas leaks, reads analog, digital and level gauges, identifies abnormal temperatures and sounds and detects partial discharge. Results appear in one monitoring interface with equipment location, site images, temperature data, gauge readings and inspection history. Because the robot repeats the same routes, it builds standardized historical data, which the company says can be extended to condition-based predictive maintenance. The system consists of the robot, sensor payloads, anomaly detection software, monitoring software and wireless communication equipment.

A-PRO says the system has been validated across the full inspection workflow, from autonomous patrol to abnormality alerts, at an operating power plant in Korea, using a communications architecture designed to meet power plant security requirements. In June 2026, it signed a memorandum of understanding with robot service company Clobot to jointly pursue robot-based autonomous safety inspection, with Clobot supplying and maintaining Boston Dynamics' Spot robots and A-PRO developing the AI algorithms, integrating the robots and handling field implementation.

The company's core business is formation and charge/discharge equipment for lithium-ion batteries, which it has supplied to production lines run by LG Energy Solution and Ultium Cells. It was listed on the KOSDAQ in 2020, has an R&D center in Siheung and has subsidiaries in Poland, China and the United States. The inspection system has not yet generated export sales.

The United States is A-PRO's main overseas target, where it plans to pursue joint demonstrations with power generation and utility companies through the Electric Power Research Institute (EPRI) programs. It also plans to expand into Poland, Hungary and Southeast Asia, including Vietnam, using its local subsidiaries and customer networks. It is seeking operation and maintenance engineering firms with direct access to customer sites, robotic system integrators that can supply and maintain quadruped robots locally and distributors of industrial safety and asset management solutions. A-PRO cites strict security rules and site access limits at overseas plants, country-specific requirements for hardware and cybersecurity, and a shortage of channels to find qualified local partners as its main challenges.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
